A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Parity-aware BPE study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original tokenizer evaluations, ablations, and downstream accuracy and perplexity results from trained 3B language models.

after.justification: V3 retains the original language-model results and reports additional tokenizer experiments, including FineWeb2 training and hyperparameter sensitivity evaluations.

M1.justification: V3 Section 4.3 introduces target-normalized language selection, CR/r_l, extending v1's unadjusted no-dev option. V1 discussed such compensation only as future work. This is a limited procedural extension: the core algorithm, hybrid and moving-window mechanisms, and encoding procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: FineWeb2 is newly used for tokenizer training alongside mC4; v1 used it for language-model training only. The 30/60-language sets and FLORES+ evaluation remain. V3 also removes XCOPA from reported benchmark coverage, changing 13 benchmarks to 12, although v1's twelve-item benchmark list and unchanged downstream scores leave an actual evaluation removal uncertain.

E2.justification: The comparison variants change within retained mC4 experiments: no-dev and hybrid+no-dev entries disappear from the corresponding tables. The external baselines remain Classical BPE and UnigramLM. In particular, UnigramLM is retained in the matched 128k/30-language comparison, moving from v1 Table 1 to v3 Table 5.

E3.justification: V1 describes unbalanced tokenizer data as proportional to mC4 quantities; v3 specifies temperature sampling with tau=3.3 for both tokenizer corpora. The reported corpus-compression metric changes from averaging per-string ratios to dividing corpus totals. New protocols vary window size and development-set size. These substantially revise the intrinsic evaluation setup without establishing which experiments were rerun; the 3B/100B-token LM setup is retained.

E4.justification: New Tables 3–4 test window sizes 50–200 and development sets of 100, 300, and 997 examples, directly examining sensitivity and parallel-data requirements previously untested. V1's script-group analysis and Figure 5 are removed, as are its unadjusted no-dev ablation results. Vocabulary-size, language-count, and data-balance analyses remain with revised results.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is reduced in matched intrinsic comparisons: compression-rate ± values disappear, and the balanced 30-language table also loses fertility and MorphScore ± values. Other mC4 tables retain those latter uncertainty terms. Downstream Table 2 retains identical standard errors; neither version establishes an increase in repeated runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Intrinsic results are extensively revised and expanded. Under revised reported protocols, the mC4 128k/30-language BPE and PA-BPE Gini values change from 0.064/0.011 in v1 Table 1 to 0.067/0.027 in v3 Table 5. New FineWeb2 Table 1 reports 0.064/0.007, and sensitivity tables add further outcomes. These are not established same-setting improvements. Downstream Table 2 and the perplexity results are retained.

T1.justification: The non-equivalent revision of corpus compression to a ratio of totals aligns the main-text definition with Algorithm 2, which already used that formula in v1. V3 also formalizes ratio-target selection and removes the explicit detokenization inverse and losslessness equation. These are localized mathematical revisions; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central fairness-without-downstream-cost contribution remains. However, v1's matching-or-exceeding language and assurance covering every tested language are narrowed to no evidence of systematic degradation and differences within standard errors for nearly all languages. V3 also presents ratio-normalized operation as a supported practical option.

C2.justification: V3 reframes downstream evaluation as a regression check and other intrinsic metrics as auxiliary diagnostics. It proposes domain mismatch as an explanation for weaker ratio-variant fairness, adds an extended argument about corpus balancing and distribution mismatch in Appendix E, and develops qualifications about targets, window constraints, and residual inequality. This substantially expands and revises the scientific interpretation.

D1.justification: V3 identifies TokEval, specifies the HuggingFace UnigramLM implementation, more precisely identifies the SwissAI Nanotron fork, adds benchmark data-access URLs, and reports HuggingFace availability for Parity-aware BPE. Hardware, training time, optimizer, and learning-rate details were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: V3 adds references including Arnett et al. on tokenizer inequities, Lesci et al. on tokenization bias, TokEval, SuperBPE, and multilingual evaluation precedents. Appendix E expands positioning relative to corpus balancing, while v1's critique of Ali et al.'s parity-performance comparison is removed. The principal related-work framework remains.

P1.justification: There is substantial rewriting across the abstract, introduction, preliminaries, experimental setup, results, conclusion, and limitations. Classical BPE becomes a standalone section, tokenization fairness receives a dedicated subsection, and the appendices are reorganized around new hyperparameter and corpus-balancing discussions. This exceeds routine editing or renumbering.

P2.justification: V3 adds FineWeb2 and sensitivity tables, restructures intrinsic tables with vocabulary-utilization columns and metric-direction indicators, and redraws resource-group plots with revised axes and legends. The per-language compression display appears in the main text with new results. Script-group and learning-rate plots are removed, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V3 directly tests window sensitivity and parallel-data requirements left untested in v1, broadens tokenizer-training evidence, aligns the compression definition with the pseudocode, and interprets unchanged downstream results more cautiously. These improve support and clarity. The net gain is limited by reporting inconsistencies: Appendix C.3's percentage reductions conflict with Table 4, and the retained balanced-data interpretation does not match the updated resource-group trends in Figure 4.
